transcript.text: Thank you all for being here. Before we review the draft election plan, I need to raise an important matter. I conducted a confidential student-safety review and found a substantiated retaliation concern involving two students in this election. Because of this, our student-privacy protocol requires anonymous voting and prohibits releasing vote totals until the election is certified. I have not yet briefed Dr. Morgan on this, but I believe we need to address these requirements before the plan moves forward for approval.

transcript.text: This is critical, Ms. Ellis, because it directly affects the anonymous voting requirement you just raised. I tested the draft online ballot this morning and found that the platform records each voter's identity for 90 days, and that recording cannot be disabled. This means the online ballot in the current draft plan cannot provide the anonymous voting your student-privacy protocol requires. The approved workaround is sealed paper ballots counted by two adults, with zero electronic voter records. I have not yet updated the election plan to reflect this since the test.

transcript.text: Thank you, Ms. Ellis and Mr. Shah. This is exactly why I asked for this review before approving the plan. It sounds like we need to revise the draft plan to use sealed paper ballots counted by two adults with zero electronic voter records, and we need to ensure vote totals are not released until the election is certified. Before I approve anything, I want to make sure we've addressed both the anonymous voting requirement and the vote-total publication issue. Are there any other concerns with the current draft plan that we need to resolve?
